title: After My Husband Spent Five Nights Away From Home, I Sent One Message to 500 Employees—Then His Lawyer Discovered the Secret Fortune He Never Knew I Had

blocks.text: The fifth night my husband failed to come home was the night I finally stopped pretending our marriage was worth saving.
For five nights, I had slept alone in our enormous house.
For five nights, I had called Aaron Prescott, only to hear the same excuse.
“Business emergency, Claire. Don’t wait up.”
Sometimes he claimed he was meeting investors. Other times, he blamed an important acquisition or an unexpected executive meeting.
By the third, I had stopped believing anything that came out of his mouth.
On the fourth night, I discovered a hotel receipt tucked inside his jacket.
And the name on the second reservation was Jasmine Cole, his executive assistant.
Jasmine was thirty-one, ambitious, beautiful, and always seemed to find reasons to touch my husband’s arm whenever we attended company functions.
I simply hadn’t wanted to believe what I was seeing.
Don’t wait up. Things are complicated. I’ll explain when I get home.
I stared at those words for nearly a minute.
I logged into the internal communications platform at Prescott Global, the company my husband had spent years presenting to the world as his greatest achievement.
There were more than 500 employees in the main company channel.
“Good morning. This is Claire Prescott. I’d like to thank Jasmine Cole for keeping my husband company. From this moment forward, Aaron no longer needs to come home.”
Within seconds, the message had been seen.
Within minutes, my phone began ringing nonstop.
For the first time in seven years, I slept peacefully.
And by sunrise, I had packed Aaron’s belongings into two suitcases.
I delivered them to Prescott Global headquarters along with a proposed divorce agreement.
I had no intention of begging him to stay.
I had something much more important to do.
And Aaron had absolutely no idea what was coming.
The Wife Everyone Underestimated
When I married Aaron seven years earlier, he was a promising businessman with enormous ambitions.
He had a small office, twelve employees, and a dream of building a company that would compete with the biggest names in the industry.
At least, that’s what everyone believed.
Aaron told people I had helped him emotionally through the difficult early years. He described me as a devoted wife who preferred staying home rather than participating in corporate life.
But he conveniently forgot one important detail.
Prescott Global had been built with money from my family’s private investment trust.

My grandmother, Eleanor Prescott, had founded a technology investment company decades earlier. Before she died, she left me a substantial fortune and controlling interests in several private businesses.
I inherited more money than most people could spend in several lifetimes.
I wanted someone to love me without looking at my bank account.
When I met Aaron, I believed he was that person.
I allowed him to believe we were building our life together from nothing.
I even let him take the public spotlight as the company’s founder and chief executive.
What he never understood was that the money financing his biggest opportunities wasn’t coming from outside investors.
Through a private holding company and a family trust, I had quietly retained 68 percent of Prescott Global’s voting shares.
And after five nights of betrayal, I was finally ready to stop protecting him.
The Morning Everything Changed
At 9:15 a.m., Aaron stormed into the executive conference room.
I calmly placed my coffee cup on the table.
“Do you have any idea what you’ve done? Five hundred employees have seen that ridiculous message!”
“Delete it! Tell everyone it was a misunderstanding!”
Aaron slammed his hand against the table.
“This is a private matter! You had no right to involve the company!”
He had spent five nights with another woman while using company resources, company accommodations, and company expenses.
“You’re right,” I said quietly. “Our marriage is a private matter. That’s why I brought your belongings here instead of leaving them on the street.”
“Jasmine, you don’t need to worry. You’re welcome to keep him company. I’ve officially resigned from that position.”
I stood, picked up my handbag, and walked toward the door.
Before leaving, I placed an envelope in front of him.
Inside was the proposed divorce agreement.
He was too busy telling me how much money I would lose if I continued behaving this way.
Because he still didn’t know what I owned.
The Lawyer’s Discovery
Two days later, Aaron arrived at my lawyer’s office with his personal attorney, Richard Bennett.
Richard was an experienced corporate lawyer who had represented Aaron in several business transactions.
He walked into the meeting looking confident.
